title: fix(ai-utils, openai-base, ai-openrouter): let the Responses body end before aborting after a terminal event

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+'@tanstack/ai-utils': patch
+---
+
+Add `drainAfterTerminal`, which the OpenAI and OpenRouter Responses adapters use to let the body end by itself after a terminal event instead of cancelling a finished request.

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+'@tanstack/openai-base': patch
+---
+
+Stop the OpenAI Responses adapters from aborting a finished request. After `response.completed` the adapters stopped reading at once, so the OpenAI SDK aborted the request and a gateway such as Cloudflare AI Gateway logged a billed, complete call as a client cancel (499). The adapters now let the body end by itself for up to 250 ms and abort it only after that.

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+'@tanstack/ai-openrouter': patch
+---
+
+Stop the OpenRouter Responses adapter from cancelling a finished request. After `response.completed` the adapter stopped reading at once, which cancelled the SDK's event stream and the fetch body, so a gateway such as Cloudflare AI Gateway logged a billed, complete call as a client cancel (499). The adapter now lets the body end by itself for up to 250 ms and cancels it only after that.

@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+/**
+ * After a terminal Responses event the adapter stops reading. That cancels the
+ * SDK's event stream and the fetch body, so a gateway logs a finished call as
+ * a client cancel (499). The adapter gives the body a short time to end by
+ * itself and only then cancels it (#1965).
+ */
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+import { HTTPClient } from '@openrouter/sdk'
+import { resolveDebugOption } from '@tanstack/ai/adapter-internals'
+import { OpenRouterResponsesTextAdapter } from '../src/adapters/responses-text'
+
+const logger = resolveDebugOption(false)
+const model = 'openai/gpt-5.5'
+const messages = [{ role: 'user' as const, content: 'Hi' }]
+const completed = {
+  type: 'response.completed',
+  sequence_number: 1,
+  response: {
+    id: 'resp-1',
+    object: 'response',
+    created_at: 0,
+    model,
+    status: 'completed',
+    output: [],
+  },
+}
+
+interface Seen {
+  cancelled: boolean
+  /** Whether the body had been cancelled when it ended by itself. */
+  cancelledAtEnd: boolean
+}
+
+/** A body that sends `completed`, then ends after `closeAfterMs` (never if null). */
+function adapterFor(closeAfterMs: number | null, seen: Seen) {
+  const httpClient = new HTTPClient({
+    fetcher: async () => {
+      const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
+        start(controller) {
+          controller.enqueue(
+            new TextEncoder().encode(`data: ${JSON.stringify(completed)}\n\n`),
+          )
+          if (closeAfterMs !== null) {
+            setTimeout(() => {
+              seen.cancelledAtEnd = seen.cancelled
+              try {
+                controller.close()
+              } catch {
+                // the body was cancelled, so it is already closed
+              }
+            }, closeAfterMs)
+          }
+        },
+        cancel() {
+          seen.cancelled = true
+        },
+      })
+      return new Response(body, {
+        headers: { 'content-type': 'text/event-stream' },
+      })
+    },
+  })
+  return new OpenRouterResponsesTextAdapter(
+    { apiKey: 'test-key', httpClient },
+    model,
+  )
+}
+
+const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms))
+
+const entries = [
+  {
+    name: 'chatStream',
+    run: async (adapter: OpenRouterResponsesTextAdapter<typeof model>) => {
+      for await (const _ of adapter.chatStream({
+        threadId: 't',
+        logger,
+        model,
+        messages,
+      })) {
+        // drain
+      }
+    },
+  },
+  {
+    name: 'structuredOutputStream',
+    run: async (adapter: OpenRouterResponsesTextAdapter<typeof model>) => {
+      for await (const _ of adapter.structuredOutputStream({
+        chatOptions: { threadId: 't', logger, model, messages },
+        outputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: { a: { type: 'number' } } },
+      })) {
+        // drain
+      }
+    },
+  },
+]
+
+describe.each(entries)('$name after response.completed', ({ run }) => {
+  it('does not cancel a body that ends by itself soon after', async () => {
+    // starts true so the test fails if the body never ends
+    const seen: Seen = { cancelled: false, cancelledAtEnd: true }
+    await run(adapterFor(20, seen))
+    await sleep(80)
+    expect(seen.cancelledAtEnd).toBe(false)
+  })
+
+  it('returns at once and cancels a body that never ends', async () => {
+    const seen: Seen = { cancelled: false, cancelledAtEnd: false }
+    await run(adapterFor(null, seen))
+    expect(seen.cancelled).toBe(false)
+    await sleep(450)
+    expect(seen.cancelled).toBe(true)
+  })
+})

@@ -0,0 +1,102 @@
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
+import { drainAfterTerminal } from '../src/drain-after-terminal'
+
+interface Event {
+  type: string
+}
+
+const type = (event: Event) => event.type
+
+/** A body that sends `events` and then stays open until closed or cancelled. */
+function body(events: Array<Event>) {
+  let close = () => {}
+  let cancelled = false
+  const stream = new ReadableStream<Event>({
+    start(controller) {
+      for (const event of events) controller.enqueue(event)
+      close = () => controller.close()
+    },
+    cancel() {
+      cancelled = true
+    },
+  })
+  return { stream, close: () => close(), cancelled: () => cancelled }
+}
+
+/** An iterable that sends `events`, then waits forever; records `abort` and `return`. */
+function iterable(events: Array<Event>) {
+  const seen = { aborted: false, returned: false }
+  const stream: AsyncIterable<Event> = {
+    [Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
+      let i = 0
+      return {
+        next: () =>
+          i < events.length
+            ? Promise.resolve({ done: false, value: events[i++]! })
+            : new Promise<IteratorResult<Event>>(() => {}),
+        return: () => {
+          seen.returned = true
+          return Promise.resolve({ done: true, value: undefined })
+        },
+      }
+    },
+  }
+  return { stream, abort: () => (seen.aborted = true), seen }
+}
+
+async function readFirst(events: AsyncIterable<Event>) {
+  for await (const _ of events) break
+}
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  vi.useFakeTimers()
+})
+afterEach(() => {
+  vi.useRealTimers()
+})
+
+describe('drainAfterTerminal', () => {
+  it.each([
+    'response.completed',
+    'response.failed',
+    'response.incomplete',
+    'error',
+  ])('does not cancel a body that ends soon after %s', async (terminal) => {
+    const b = body([{ type: terminal }])
+    await readFirst(drainAfterTerminal(b.stream, type))
+    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(100)
+    b.close()
+    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(500)
+    expect(b.cancelled()).toBe(false)
+  })
+
+  it('cancels a body that has not ended 250 ms after a terminal event', async () => {
+    const b = body([{ type: 'response.completed' }])
+    await readFirst(drainAfterTerminal(b.stream, type))
+    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(249)
+    expect(b.cancelled()).toBe(false)
+    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1)
+    expect(b.cancelled()).toBe(true)
+  })
+
+  it('cancels at once on a stop after a non-terminal event', async () => {
+    const b = body([{ type: 'response.output_text.delta' }])
+    await readFirst(drainAfterTerminal(b.stream, type))
+    expect(b.cancelled()).toBe(true)
+  })
+
+  it('aborts an iterable 250 ms after a terminal event', async () => {
+    const src = iterable([{ type: 'response.completed' }])
+    await readFirst(drainAfterTerminal(src.stream, type, src.abort))
+    expect(src.seen.aborted).toBe(false)
+    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(250)
+    expect(src.seen.aborted).toBe(true)
+    expect(src.seen.returned).toBe(false)
+  })
+
+  it('closes an iterable at once when it has no abort', async () => {
+    const src = iterable([{ type: 'response.completed' }])
+    await readFirst(drainAfterTerminal(src.stream, type))
+    expect(src.seen.returned).toBe(true)
+  })
+})
